featured_reviews.name: Rohan Kini
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited this place on a weekday morning for breakfast. The menu covers all the South Indian staples—idli, dosa, paniyaram, filter coffee, sheera—so there’s a good variety to choose from.

Seating is limited and small , it can hold a capacity of 15 -20 people thats it .

We ordered ghee podi idli, benne dosa,rasam wada and paniyaram. Everything was served fresh and hot, as they start preparing the food only after the order is placed. The filter coffee takes a little time to be prepared, so it’s better to order accordingly. Tea lovers should note that tea is not available here.

Coming to the quality and quantity: the food is slightly on the oilier side, which may feel heavy for those not used to that style. Taste-wise, it was good—the idlis were soft, the dosas were crisp the rasam wada was throat touching and the filter coffee was spot on.

featured_reviews.name: Gitesh More
featured_reviews.review_text:
I ordered food from Oota Thindi, Borivali West, and was extremely disappointed by the excessive amount of oil used in the dish. The curry was literally floating in oil, making it unpleasant to eat and raising serious health concerns.

Traditional food does not mean food should be drenched in oil. Such cooking practices are unsafe for regular consumption, especially for customers mindful of cholesterol, heart health, and overall well-being. The taste was completely overpowered by oil, and a large portion had to be discarded.

Restaurants have a responsibility towards their customers’ health. I genuinely hope Oota Thindi takes this feedback seriously and improves its cooking standards. Until then, I would strongly advise the restaurant to control oil usage and maintain healthier food quality.

featured_reviews.name: Raj Arunachala
featured_reviews.review_text:
Classic example of how great food can be ruined by absolutely horrific service!

Oota Thindi, serving Pan South Indian cuisine is a sure-shot candidate for one of those restaurant makeover shows!

From the get go, the reservation process starts off in confusion. The person managing the front desk is absolutely clueless about taking reservations and then subsequently calling people. I kept a tab on him that’s why I was able to get a table!

Having arrived at the table, the waiting staff is completely clueless. It took a really long time before someone came to take order. Our waiter was knowledgeable about the menu though. And made some great suggestions.

The menu is another disaster with too many options that most people aren’t even familiar with. Even being a south Indian who lives in Tamil Nadu, some of menu items were confusing. A simple classification of Starters, Main course etc is preferred.

We ordered some starters which arrived on time. As for the rest of our courses, the wait time was painstakingly long. The waiters have no clue what’s going on with orders. And there are too many of them mulling around avoiding talking to customers.

So many other customers were also getting frustrated by the delays. One person even yelled at the manager! Though he just shrugged it off and walked away!

The food is the only redeeming factor as is the nicely done ambience. Although the main hall is too brightly lit for dinner.

I find myself reluctant to recommend this place despite the good food because of the appalling service! How is it so hard in Mumbai?!
Just hire some very capable Shetty people who have mastered the art of running a South Indian restaurant!

Overall, a very disappointing experience at Oota Thindi!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Oota Thindi and had an absolutely wonderful dining experience that I just had to share!

I ordered a variety of dishes that showcased the authentic flavors of South Indian cuisine, and each one was a treat:

Benne Ellu Podi Dosa (INR 290) - This was the star of my meal! The butter and sesame powder combination created such a rich, nutty flavor that perfectly complemented the crispy dosa. Absolutely divine!

Thali (INR 695 )-  An excellent value for money! The thali was well-portioned with a great variety of dishes that gave me a complete taste of traditional South Indian flavors.

Thenga Manga Sundal (INR 225) - A refreshing and healthy option with coconut and raw mango. The tanginess was just right, making it a perfect side dish.

Thakali Thokku Brahmin Style Idli (INR 225 ) - Soft, fluffy idlis paired with the flavorful tomato thokku. This Brahmin-style preparation was authentic and delicious!

Kalyana Rasam (INR 245 ) - The wedding-style rasam was aromatic and soul-warming. Perfect comfort food!

The total came to INR 1,780 , which I found very reasonable considering the quality and quantity of food. The ordering system was modern and user-friendly, and the service was efficient.

If you're craving authentic South Indian cuisine, Oota Thindi is definitely the place to go. I'll definitely be returning to try more items from their menu!

Highly recommended! 👌

featured_reviews.review_text:

The décor and ambiance are thoughtfully done, with colors and symbols that reflect the essence of South India. The food overall was decent. I especially enjoyed the Pongal rice, dal vada, and their signature filter coffee. The chutneys were fresh and flavorful, and the pineapple sheera was a delightful sweet ending.
On the flip side, the idlis could have been softer and the medu vada (Ulundu) crispier. The sambar was served lukewarm initially, but when I requested a hot one, the staff promptly obliged—which speaks well of their service.
Overall, Oota Thindi is worth a visit if you want to relish authentic South Indian flavors in Borivali.

featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
Now that Benne Dosa is so much in trend, I decided to look for a nearby outlet and try it out, so I visited Namma Benne House, Taste the Authenticity of Bengaluru. This outlet is located in Borivali West near Croma.

This is a self service setup with only outdoor seating, so the focus here is clearly on the food. I ordered Ghee Pudi Idli and Benne Plain Dosa.

The Ghee Pudi Idli was served hot and fresh. The texture was very good. It was soft and moist. It was soft, moist, and evenly coated with ghee and plenty of pudi.

The Benne Plain Dosa was not very crispy. It was more on the softer side. I feel it was made using a different style of batter. The fermentation was good. The dosa was cooked evenly. The ghee added richness without making it oily.
It was served with sambar and two types of chutneys, both of which were well balanced and complemented the dosa well. The sambar was delicious.

The menu mentions that potato palya is included with every dosa. I was not served that. This affected the overall experience. The prices are on the higher side, and for a self service outlet, I would have expected slightly better value.

That said, I genuinely appreciated their effort towards sustainability. They are using eco friendly plates and spoons, and I did not notice any plastic being used, which is a thoughtful touch.

If you want to try a Bengaluru style Benne Dosa, you can visit Namma Benne House in Borivali.

I always try to treat my parents to something special when I get a chance. That’s why I decided to visit this South Indian café near the Borivali railway station with them. I came all the way from Navsari, Gujarat, and I was a bit skeptical at first, but this place completely won me over.
The dosa was absolutely spot‑on — the most authentic taste I’ve had outside of traditional South Indian restaurants. I also tried their filter coffee, and it was very nice and genuinely authentic, just like the ones I’ve had in South India. The service was friendly and attentive, and the interiors felt like they fell straight out of a Pinterest board: clean, cozy, and very welcoming.
I was personally assisted by Mr. Radhe, who was very helpful and patient with us. He suggested the “100‑year‑old dosa” from their menu, and it turned out to be a fantastic choice. My parents loved it, and I was really happy seeing them enjoy the food. It made the whole trip feel worth it.

One small thing: the reception area had quite a few mosquitoes, even though they were using mosquito repellent. It was a bit hard to sit there comfortably. On the other hand, the toilet was very clean and well‑maintained, so if anyone wants to freshen up, it is a good place.
I’ll definitely visit again whenever I’m in Bombay. Strongly recommended for anyone looking for genuine South Indian flavors, good filter coffee, and warm hospitality!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Malgudi: Great Vibes, Confused Kitchen & Extra Fees
Let’s be real—I wanted to love this place. Walking into Malgudi on SV Road, the vibe is immaculate. It sets you up for a cozy, authentic South Indian experience. But between the kitchen confusion and the final bill, it’s a bit of a rollercoaster.
Here is the unfiltered breakdown:
The Star of the Show
If you go here, do yourself a favor and order the Benne Masala Dosa. It was genuinely too good—crispy, buttery, and exactly what you hope for. The chutney pairing was also on point and very tasty.
The "What happened here?" Section
Unfortunately, the rest of the meal felt like an identity crisis.
• The Sambar Situation: This was weird. The sambar actually tasted different across different dishes. Consistency is key, guys—pick a lane!
• Portions & Options: The menu feels very limited, and the portion sizes are basically a tease. For the price, you expect to leave full, not looking for a snack on the way home.
• Overall Taste: Aside from the Benne Dosa, the general taste could really be improved. It feels like they are holding back flavor.
The Coffee Letdown
For a place with this vibe, you expect the coffee game to be strong. It wasn't.
• Coffee Mocktails: Hard pass. They just felt not worth the price tag.
• Filter Coffee: The ultimate test for a South Indian spot, and they failed it. It tasted average at best and definitely lacked that authentic "kick" you crave.
The Final Pinch
Just when you are questioning the portion sizes vs. the price, the bill arrives. They levy a 5% Service Charge.
Paying extra for "service" when the filter coffee is average and the sambar is inconsistent? That stings.
The Verdict
Go for the Benne Masala Dosa and the aesthetic, but lower your expectations for everything else. It’s a great place to sit, but be ready to pay a premium (plus 5%) for a mixed bag of flavors.

featured_reviews.name: BhataktiAatmaWasHere
featured_reviews.review_text:
Āhāra (आहार) in Sanskrit simply means food—nourishment for the body and, if done right, the soul too. Bright and early, we paid a visit to Aahara for exactly that, and let’s just say … it understood the assignment.

The space is thoroughly Instagrammable (because clearly we eat with our eyes first), the service impressively prompt for the morning hour, and the food, comforting in the best possible way. The idlis were pillowy soft, the kind that politely ask the chutney for company. The upma was moist, flavourful, and thankfully far removed from the dry, crumbly versions that have given upma a bad reputation.

Then came the Bangalore-style Benne Dosa: thick, indulgent, and utterly unapologetic. Cooked generously in white butter, it strikes that magical balance: crisp on the outside, softly fermented within, and fragrant enough to make nearby tables curious. Served with a spicy chutney and potato palya—Karnataka’s no-nonsense potato stir-fry of soft, lightly mashed potatoes, onions, green chillies and curry leaves, it’s a dosa that firmly believes butter is a food group 😂

The chutneys were the familiar trio but thicker—no watery business here—and the sambhar, though sans vegetables, was rich, thick, and deeply satisfying, proving that simplicity often gets it right.

All in all, Aahara delivered āhāra in its truest sense—simple, nourishing, and deeply comforting. Food that doesn’t shout for attention, yet leaves you well-fed, well-pleased, and quietly planning your next visit.

featured_reviews.name: Ronit Gaikwad
featured_reviews.review_text:
We were looking to have lunch and thought of trying out food at Dwarka. The restaurant is near the Borivali Railway station and has AC and non-AC sections.

We started by ordering masala papad. The papad was as is regularly found in restaurants. A fried crunchy papad topped off with some chilli powder and chat masala, along with a garnishing of freshly chopped tomatoes, onions, and coriander. The taste was delicious, and the good part being it was not too spicy. The papad was indeed a light starter to the main course.

For the main course, we tried out their Punjabi thali. The thali had three vegetables - paneer butter masala, mixed vegetables, and a dry sabzi which we replaced with mixed veg. to make it double. Both dishes were delicious, and, for my thali, they took care to give me both sabzis without coriander and garlic, right in line with the special instructions. We order roti with one and naan with another thali. I had the butter naan, which was delicious, with a generous quantity of butter flowing through it. I found it exceptionally soft; the best part is that the naan was not even slightly burnt, indicating it was cooked perfectly.

The dal fry and the tawa pulav were cooked very well, and in fact, the tawa pulav was one of the best I have had in many restaurants. Made with long-grained rice, it was not too spicy but just enough to bring out the flavor of the spices used with the rice. Lastly, the gulab jamun was served hot and was just perfectly sweet to end the entire lunch with a dessert.

All in all, we thoroughly enjoyed our lunch at the restaurant. Correct quantity, great taste, and professional service. I would recommend visiting the restaurant.

Visited this pure veg restaurant on a Sunday night, and it was quite crowded with a waiting time. Since we were just two people, we got a table immediately.
We placed our order, but the service was extremely slow. Even for something as basic as water glasses, we had to wait around 10 minutes and remind them multiple times, which was disappointing.
Coming to the food, We ordered Masala Papad, Manchow Soup, Spring Rolls, and Pav Bhaji. The Masala Papad was good, and the Manchow Soup was flavourful, served hot with crispy fried noodles. The Spring Rolls were well-prepared, perfectly crunchy on the outside with a fresh and well-cooked filling. The Schezwan chutney served along with it was also very tasty.
However, the Pav Bhaji was a letdown. The bhaji lacked proper spices and had large chunks of unsmashed potato, which affected the overall taste. I wouldn’t recommend ordering it here.
Overall, the food was decent except for the Pav Bhaji, but the service really needs improvement. It was slow, and even after informing the staff multiple times, there was a lack of attention.

featured_reviews.name: kaushal vyas
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are looking for a reliable dining spot just a stone's throw away from Borivali Station (West), Radhakrishna Hotel is a solid choice. I visited this place last Sunday, and its proximity to the station—literally a 2 to 3-minute walk—makes it incredibly convenient for commuters and locals alike.
Ambiance & Seating
The restaurant is split into two sections. While the ground floor handles the quick-service crowd, the AC section is located on the 1st floor. The climb is worth it, as the upstairs area offers a decent ambiance that is much more relaxed and comfortable for a family dinner or a quiet lunch. The cooling was effective, providing a welcome escape from the Mumbai heat.
Service & Accessibility
One thing to keep in mind is the limited parking space. Given its location in a high-traffic area near the station, finding a spot for a four-wheeler can be a struggle; it is definitely better suited for those arriving by foot or rickshaw.
Final Verdict
The food remains consistent with the classic Udipi-style quality one expects from the Radhakrishna brand. Whether you’re stopping by for a quick South Indian breakfast or a full North Indian meal in the AC section, it offers good value for money. It is a dependable, no-fuss establishment that excels in convenience and comfort.

featured_reviews.name: Sania Serrao
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hotel Radha Krishna in Borivali is a cozy, no-frills eatery that’s a favorite among lovers of authentic South Indian cuisine. The ambience is simple and welcoming, making it perfect for casual breakfasts, family meals, or a quick bite with friends.

The menu features classic South Indian staples — from crisp dosas and soft idlis to flavorful sambhar, chutneys, and wholesome thalis. Every dish is prepared with care, balancing authentic taste with generous portions that leave you fully satisfied.

Service is friendly and efficient, keeping the experience pleasant and hassle-free. Hotel Radha Krishna is the kind of place you visit for comfort, quality, and that familiar home-style South Indian flavor that keeps people coming back.
